title: How I used AI to price footballers

guide: This guide shows how to point machine learning at football. You need a laptop, a free ChatGPT or Claude account (or Codex or Claude Code), and a football dataset you can download.
1. Pick one of the two projects: predict a player's market value, or predict the formation the other team will play.
1. Find a public Premier League dataset, such as a downloadable CSV of player stats and market values or of match lineups, and save it in a Google Drive folder.
1. Ask ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code to open the file and describe the columns, the missing values and what each row represents.
1. Decide what you are predicting (the market value, or the formation) and which columns the model may use as inputs.
1. Ask the assistant to split the data into training and test sets, then train a simple model in Python with scikit-learn.
1. Compare the model's predictions with the real values on the test set and ask the assistant to explain which inputs mattered most.
1. Improve one thing at a time, such as adding a new input or trying a different model, and re-run the same comparison.
1. Put the results in a chart and a short write-up so someone else can follow what you did.
Watch out: Premier League data is far easier to find than lower-league data, so start there, and never judge the model on the same rows it trained on.
